record.title: Built for support, turned into profit
record.body:
I’ve used this app for years to track my self-harm recovery, and it’s been genuinely meaningful to me. Having the widget on my lock screen and watching the days increase has been a huge source of motivation.

That’s why I’m really disappointed to see widgets moved behind a paywall, especially one that isn’t particularly affordable. As a loyal user, it doesn’t feel right to have features that were previously free taken away.

I understand charging for new features, but removing existing ones, especially from an app people rely on for personal and vulnerable reasons, feels unfair. I hope this change is reconsidered or that long-term users are taken into account.

source: Research/App Store Reviews/43. Habit Hub - Routine Tracker - Daily Todo, Goals & Schedule/reviews.jsonl

record.title: This system keeps me functional!
record.body:
I have ASD and have some executive functioning issues which have been exacerbated during the pandemic. I tried a few other apps to keep me on task/on schedule and found it was too easy for me to ignore them. But this app? This app works! 
1) I love that it’s a widget! I can see what I need to do right from the home screen without having to open the app. That’s super helpful! Because of my EF issues, if I have to seek it out a lot of the time it’s not happening. I can miss notifications, but not if it’s on my Home Screen. 
2) Thank you for %’s and grades. This is how my brain works. Since I’ve put a daily exercise routine as one of my tasks, I’m actually completing it so I can stay at a 90% “grade”. This is the first year I’ve actually stuck out a workout routine because of it! 
3) I can keep track of tasks that are weekly, monthly, etc. Instead of wondering the last time I cleaned out the fridge, I can check the app. I feel like I’m on top of things instead of drowning in a bunch of stuff that needs to be done or hasn’t been done in months since I keep forgetting about it. 
This app has been literally life changing for me. I feel much more in control of my own life and home in ways that I never have before. Thank you so, so much!

source: Research/App Store Reviews/53. HabitMinder • Habit Tracker - Daily Reminders & Routines/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Outstanding - almost there
record.body:
Habit apps are a crowded marketplace, and this one really stands out to me. Gorgeous design that is very simple and easy on the eyes, but still very flexible. They found the right balance. It’s engaging and fun to check things off (might as well use the addictiveness of technology to help your productivity :) Their hydration app is equally fantastic. Both have earned a permanent spot in my “Today” view...assuming a few things are in the works. 

1. Mac app - visibility and management of tasks/habits is really only viable if you can access them (and synced notifications) from any device. 

2. The notification text is a bit odd. I wish these would just contain the habit text and nothing else. They often appear as verbose sentences that you have to read. For me this affects the fluidity of use. 

3. The Today widget could be enhanced by only showing remaining habits at the top. 

4. Ability both to skip habits or mark as failed would be nice. 

Items 2–4 are all ways of helping you see only what you need to see. The “at a glance” nature of this app isn’t quite there yet. 

The comments seem to indicate that more integration with multiple devices is forthcoming. Lack of this functionality is normally a dealbreaker for me, but I’m using this on my phone only for the moment because the app is just that good. At whatever point these become more integrated in the ecosystem, this and WaterMinder will unquestionably be 5 star software.

My ADHD makes organisation challenging and over the year I’ve tried countless apps that claim to help “neurodivergent people” or be “perfect for those who procrastinate.” They end up being made for quick cash grabs or having a wildly confusing interface that is overwhelming and challenging to navigate. 

With Dots, you get exactly what you download. All your habits trackable in a range of formats (card, list, calendar form) so you can check them off in the one you prefer. You can also add the widget to your home screen so you can cross habits off during the day without having to open the app. There’s no paywall, no ads, and it’s beautifully minimalistic. Everything I needed I am so thankful that I found this.
